title: TiL/BlackRock agree $22.8bn deal for CK Hutchison's 43 non-China ports; deal stalled through 2026
summary: A consortium of BlackRock/GIP and MSC's Terminal Investment Limited agreed to buy 80% of Hutchison Ports' 43 terminals (199 berths, 23 countries) plus 90% of Panama Ports Company for an enterprise value of $22.8bn, which Drewry said would make MSC the world's largest terminal operator. Exclusivity lapsed in July 2025 after Chinese regulatory opposition; COSCO sought a controlling role, Panama voided the Balboa/Cristobal concession in Feb 2026, and by March 2026 the consortium was reported to be pursuing a deal for ~41 ports excluding Panama. As of Oct 2026 no closing had been announced, though MSC and Hutchison resumed talks on Rotterdam's Omega terminal. Directly relevant to DP World: would hand MSC control of competing hubs in Sohar, Dammam, Jeddah, Karachi, Dar es Salaam and across Europe.

title: TiL to buy 49% of Adani's Vizhinjam port for $1.4bn in $2.85bn deal
summary: APSEZ and MSC Group announced that TiL will acquire a 49% interest in Adani Vizhinjam Port Pvt Ltd, the concessionaire of India's first deepwater transhipment port, investing USD 1.397bn (its share of a USD 2.85bn total deal value), subject to regulatory approvals. Vizhinjam handled 1.3m TEU in FY26 and capacity is to rise 3.5x from 1.6m to 5.7m TEU by Dec 2028. Described as the largest foreign private investment in Indian port infrastructure; it is the third APSEZ-MSC JV after Mundra CT3 and Ennore and anchors MSC's Indian Ocean transhipment strategy in competition with Colombo, Jebel Ali and Salalah.

title: MSC completes acquisition of 49.9% of HHLA, forming strategic JV with City of Hamburg
summary: MSC Group, via Port of Hamburg Beteiligungsgesellschaft SE, completed its voluntary tender offer and now holds 49.9% of Hamburger Hafen und Logistik AG, with the City of Hamburg retaining 50.1%, after Hamburg parliament approval and merger clearances. MSC committed to lift its throughput at HHLA terminals to at least 1.0m TEU/yr from 2031, the partners will inject EUR 450m of equity for investment, and MSC will build a German HQ in HafenCity (~700 staff, construction from 2026). The deal gives MSC a stake in HHLA's terminals in Hamburg, Tallinn, Trieste and Odessa and in rail operator Metrans.
partners: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg

title: Marsa Maroc finalises TiL entry (50% minus one share) into Nador West Med container terminal
summary: Following a partnership agreement signed in February 2025 and approval by the competent authorities, Marsa Maroc completed TiL's entry into West Med Container Terminal (WMCT), the company for the eastern container terminal at Nador West Med. Marsa Maroc keeps 50% plus one share; TiL holds 50% minus one share. The terminal will have 1,520 m of quay, 18 m draught and 70 ha, reaching 3.4m TEU at full build; first-phase operations are planned for Q4 2026. This creates a new MSC transhipment hub in the western Mediterranean directly competing with Tanger Med and Algeciras.
capacity: 3.4m TEU at full capacity; 1,520 m quay, 18 m draught

title: MSC Group wins 45-year concession for new container terminal at Snake Island Port, Lagos
summary: MSC Group signed a 45-year concession with Nigerdock to develop, operate and maintain a new container terminal inside the 85 ha Snake Island Port in Lagos, part of an announced investment of over USD 1bn in Nigerian port and logistics infrastructure. Design: 910 m quay for STS and mobile harbour cranes serving deep-sea vessels and barges, -16.5 m CD dredged depth scalable to -18 m, 30 ha yard with hybrid RTGs. ITB Nigeria and DEME hold the EPC contract with completion targeted for 2028. It sets up a direct rival to APM Terminals Apapa and the Lekki deep-sea port in Nigeria's main gateway.
capacity: 910 m quay; 30 ha yard; -16.5 m CD

title: TiL takes interim operation of Cristobal terminal after Panama voids Hutchison concession
summary: After Panama's Supreme Court declared the Panama Ports Company contract law unconstitutional (ruling 30 Jan 2026, published 23 Feb 2026), the government took control of Balboa and Cristobal and appointed APM Terminals to run Balboa (Pacific) and MSC's TiL to run Cristobal (Atlantic) under temporary contracts of up to 18 months while a new concession model and international tender are designed. CK Hutchison launched international arbitration. The move positions TiL for the permanent tender on the Atlantic side of the Canal, where it already holds 42.5% of PSA Panama International Terminal.

title: TiL withdraws EU merger filing for joint control of Hutchison's BEST terminal in Barcelona after Phase II probe
summary: TiL and Hutchison Ports notified the European Commission on 5 Nov 2025 of a deal giving TiL joint control of Terminal Catalunya (operator of Barcelona Europe South Terminal, ~2.8m TEU in 2025). The Commission opened an in-depth Phase II investigation on 10 Dec 2025 over concerns MSC could foreclose rival carriers at BEST, and in early August 2026 the parties withdrew the notification. The outcome shows EU antitrust limits on MSC's vertical integration and is a precedent for other carrier-controlled terminal deals in Europe.

title: Turkish competition authority clears TiL's 50% stake in SOCAR Aliaga container terminal
summary: Turkey's competition board approved TiL's acquisition of 50% of SOCAR Aliaga Liman Isletmeciligi A.S. from SOCAR Turkey Enerji, following a strategic cooperation agreement signed in Izmir on 16 Sep 2025 and an EU simplified merger review opened 29 Jan 2026 (joint control by Terminal Investment Switzerland and SOCAR Turkey). SOCAR Terminal at Aliaga is described as the largest container port in the Aegean region. The deal extends MSC/TiL's Turkish footprint beyond Asyaport and Marport.

title: Dunkerque Port selects TiL to develop and operate second container terminal (West Port)
summary: Grand Port Maritime de Dunkerque signed a reservation protocol (promise of terminal agreement) with Terminal Investment Limited Holding S.A. on 15 July 2026, under a board decision of 6 July, for the fitting-out and operation of a new container terminal at the West Port; the port board formally confirmed TiL as operator in late September 2026. The call for expressions of interest (Nov 2025) targeted ~1.5m TEU of additional capacity (1,000 m quay, 62 ha), taking Dunkirk to 2.5m TEU, with operations from around 2029 under the EUR 303m CAP 2020 programme. It gives MSC a second French gateway alongside its Le Havre terminals.

title: TiL Gdynia is sole bidder for PLN 5bn Gdynia Outer Port PPP
summary: When offers closed on 30 Sep 2026, MSC-linked Terminal Investment Limited Gdynia was the only one of four shortlisted groups to bid for the Port of Gdynia Outer Port PPP, a PLN 5bn (~EUR 1.15bn / USD 1.3bn) deep-water, NATO dual-use terminal described as Poland's largest PPP. Other shortlisted parties (Hutchison Ports/Felixstowe, Mota-Engil/CCCC, ICTSI) did not submit. The port authority has 90 days to assess the offer. A win would give MSC a new Baltic hub next to ICTSI's BCT Gdynia.

title: TiL acquires Terminal Portuario Paracas (Puerto General San Martin, Pisco) for ~$200m
summary: TiL agreed in December 2025 to take full ownership of Terminal Portuario de Paracas, concessionaire of Puerto General San Martin in Pisco, Peru, for a reported ~USD 200m; regulatory approval followed in February 2026 and the port began the 2026/27 grape export season under TiL. The deal adds a Peruvian multipurpose/reefer gateway to MSC's Latin American network alongside Callao and complements MSC's Wilson Sons acquisition in Brazil.

title: Namport hands Walvis Bay container terminal to TiL subsidiary under 25-year concession
summary: Namport announced in September 2024 that operations of the new Walvis Bay container terminal (commissioned 2019, 750,000 TEU/yr) passed to Terminal Investment Namibia, a TiL subsidiary, from 1 October 2024 under a 25-year concession first awarded in 2022. TiL committed to upgrades including entrance-channel dredging and new equipment. It makes MSC the gateway operator for Namibia and the Walvis Bay corridors to Botswana, Zambia and DRC, competing with DP World's Southern Africa logistics and AGL's Lobito.

title: MSC/TiL to build dedicated container terminal at Port of Aarhus; 430 m quay under construction
summary: Port of Aarhus signed a land-lease with MSC under which TiL will establish and operate a new container terminal on ~170,000 m2 of the Omniterminal area, giving Denmark's largest commercial port two major box terminals (the other run by APM Terminals). Construction of the final 430 m quay (14 m depth) by MT Hojgaard started after summer 2025 for completion end-2026, with the terminal fully developed by 2027. MSC also launched a direct Aarhus-Asia service. A direct challenge to Maersk/APMT in its home market.
capacity: ~170,000 m2 site; 430 m quay, 14 m depth

title: TiL raises $2.5bn in privately placed bonds
summary: Terminal Investment Ltd, controlled by the Aponte family's MSC Group, raised USD 2.5bn through a privately placed bond sale in USD and EUR tranches with maturities of 7, 10, 12 and 20 years, one of the largest private debt deals in the ports sector. The funding strengthens TiL's capacity to finance its expansion pipeline (Vizhinjam, Nador West Med, Dunkirk, Aarhus, Hutchison portfolio) at a time of intense competition for terminal assets.

title: MSC completes acquisition of controlling stake in Wilson Sons (towage, terminals, shipyard) for ~$790m
summary: SAS Shipping Agencies Services, a wholly owned MSC subsidiary, completed the purchase of about 56-68% of Wilson Sons after Brazilian regulators cleared the deal in May 2025; the October 2024 agreement valued the controlling stake at BRL 4.35bn (~USD 765-790m). Wilson Sons runs one of Latin America's largest tug fleets, the Tecon Rio Grande and Tecon Salvador container terminals, offshore support bases and a shipyard in Guaruja. The acquisition gives MSC an integrated towage/terminal/shipyard platform in Brazil, overlapping with the marine-services space where DP World's P&O Maritime and Svitzer compete.

title: Medlog acquires UK's Maritime Transport (Maritime Group), 1,600 trucks and 30+ daily rail services
summary: MSC's inland logistics arm MEDLOG completed the acquisition of Maritime Group Ltd, the UK's largest container haulier with ~3,000 staff, 41 sites, 1,600 trucks and a network of strategic rail freight terminals running 30+ daily trains to major UK ports; price undisclosed. Maritime had earlier been named operator of the West Midlands Strategic Rail Freight Interchange. The deal, following Medlog's iPort Rail lease in Doncaster, gives MSC end-to-end landside control in the UK, where it would also inherit Felixstowe under the Hutchison deal.

title: Medlog takes long lease of iPort Rail Phase 2 in Doncaster, doubling terminal capacity
summary: MEDLOG signed a long lease of the newly built Phase 2 of the iPort Rail intermodal terminal at Doncaster (developer Verdion), extending the operation it took over in February 2024. Phase 2 doubles storage capacity and increases the number of daily trains the terminal can handle; the hub receives block trains from Felixstowe, Southampton, Immingham and Teesport. Part of MSC's build-out of an owned UK inland network.

title: Medlog buys 50% of Ukrainian intermodal operator N'UNIT and 25% of Mostyska border rail terminal
summary: Medlog SA acquired 50% of N'UNIT, which runs four intermodal terminals (Vyshneve/Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Lviv region) and two grain warehouses, and 25% of the Mostyska cross-border gauge-change rail terminal near the Polish border, from TIS co-owner Yegor Grebennikov (Lemtrans holds 50% of Mostyska). Forbes Ukraine estimated the value at USD 15-30m, the largest logistics deal in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion. Positions MSC for Ukraine's land corridors and reconstruction cargo.

title: MSC/Medlog nears 50/50 rail freight JV with Renfe to take over most of Renfe Mercancias
summary: After Renfe's board selected Medlog as strategic partner (over Maersk and CMA CGM) to revive its loss-making freight arm, MSC was reported in May 2026 to be close to a non-binding agreement for a 50/50 JV that would absorb most Renfe Mercancias services and ~945 staff, operated via Medlog's rail unit Medway; Renfe would keep a small strategic fleet. Still subject to government approval and union opposition. Would give MSC control of Spain's largest rail freight operator, linking Valencia, Barcelona (BEST) and Algeciras hinterlands.

title: MSC launches Afungi Shuttle coastal feeder from Nacala and Maputo to northern Mozambique LNG site
summary: MSC introduced a dedicated coastal feeder, the Afungi Shuttle, with Nacala-Afungi-Nacala and Maputo-Afungi-Maputo rotations to move construction materials, machinery and spares for the Mozambique LNG project under a single MSC booking. It opens a new maritime gateway to Cabo Delgado and leverages MSC's Mozambique presence (including AGL's Nacala and Pemba terminals), in a corridor where DP World operates Maputo container terminal.

title: MSC signs MoU with Egypt's Holding Company for Maritime and Land Transport on ports, dry ports and rail freight
summary: MSC and Egypt's state Holding Company for Maritime and Land Transport signed an MoU, attended by Deputy PM Kamel El-Wazir, to cooperate on seaport and dry port operations, railway freight and logistics infrastructure to position Egypt as a regional trade hub under Vision 2030. No projects or amounts were specified. Signals MSC interest in Egyptian logistics zones where DP World (Sokhna) and AD Ports are active.
partners: Holding Company for Maritime and Land Transport (Egypt)

title: MSC and Hutchison Ports resume talks on Rotterdam Omega terminal (Maasvlakte I)
summary: Dutch unions reported that MSC and Hutchison Ports resumed negotiations, paused since July 2026, over the Omega container terminal site at Maasvlakte I in Rotterdam; the Port of Rotterdam Authority wants clarity before 1 January 2027. The talks run in parallel with the stalled global Hutchison-TiL transaction and would give MSC dedicated capacity in Europe's largest port.

title: ICTSI signs 25-year partnership with Transnet for Durban Container Terminal Pier 2; operations from 1 Jan 2026
summary: ICTSI, preferred bidder since July 2023, signed a 25-year agreement with Transnet SOC to operate and develop DCT Pier 2 (1,760 m of quay, 120 ha), South Africa's largest terminal handling >70% of Durban's and ~46% of the country's container cargo, through a Transnet-majority Newco. Targets: capacity from 2.0m to 2.8m TEU, gross crane moves/hour from 18 to 28, ship working hours from 60 to 120. ICTSI took over management on 1 January 2026 (branded Durban Gateway Terminal). A major loss for rival bidders and a new entrant on DP World's doorstep in Southern Africa.

title: ICTSI secures 25-year extension of Manila International Container Terminal concession to 2063
summary: ICTSI and the Philippine Ports Authority signed a renewal extending the MICT concession, the group's flagship, by 25 years from May 2038 to May 2063. MICT's capacity is projected to reach 3.7m TEU by 2027 under an ongoing modernisation (electric quay cranes, automation) partly financed by a USD 300m AIIB loan. Secures ICTSI's home cash engine for four decades.

title: VICT Melbourne concession extended 26 years to 2066 after approvals satisfied
summary: ICTSI's Victoria International Container Terminal (Webb Dock East, Australia's first fully automated terminal) met all conditions for a 26-year extension of its agreement with Port of Melbourne, moving expiry from 2040 to 2066 (~40 years remaining). An expansion due late 2026 lifts capacity to ~1.6m TEU; ICTSI says no significant further capex is needed, supporting cash generation and ROIC.

title: ICTSI buys HSIM, operator of two agri-bulk terminals at Aratu Port (Bahia), for ~$130m
summary: ICTSI Americas B.V. agreed to acquire 100% of HSIM Participacoes e Holding, holder of long-term public lease rights for the adjacent ATU12 and ATU18 terminals at Aratu Port, Bahia, which handle agricultural imports and exports, from SIMPAR S.A. and CS Brasil for BRL 650m (~USD 130m) plus a potential BRL 100m earn-out within 18 months. It diversifies ICTSI into dry bulk in Brazil alongside its Rio, Suape and Rio Grande container operations.

title: ICTSI sells 51% stake in Yantai International Container Terminal to Yantai Port Holdings for RMB 773m
summary: ICTSI (Hong Kong) Ltd sold its entire 51% interest (384.5m shares) in Yantai International Container Terminal to co-investor Yantai Port Holdings for RMB 773.2m (~PHP 6.76bn, ~USD 107m). ICTSI said it is focusing on concessions where it controls operational, development and commercial decisions and will redeploy capital to its pipeline. The deconsolidation reduced reported EMEA/Asia volumes in 2026.

title: AIIB lends ICTSI $300m for MICT, South Luzon and Mindanao terminal expansions
summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank provided a USD 300m senior unsecured corporate loan, its first non-sovereign-backed deal in the Philippines, to fund expansion and modernisation of Manila International Container Terminal (to ~3.7m TEU by 2027), South Luzon Container Terminal in Batangas (to 800,000 TEU by 2028) and Mindanao Container Terminal (to ~1m TEU by 2028), including fully electric quay cranes and replacement of diesel yard equipment.

title: ICTSI wins 25-year extensions to 2058 for Subic NCT-1 and NCT-2, pledges $130m
summary: Subic Bay International Terminals Corp and ICTSI Subic Inc signed 25-year extensions with the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority for New Container Terminals 1 and 2 in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, running to 2058. SBICT will invest over USD 130m to replace four quay cranes, add a fifth and deploy more hybrid RTGs, lifting combined capacity from 600,000 to 1m TEU.

title: Mindanao Container Terminal concession extended 25 years to 2058 with $100m+ upgrade
summary: ICTSI subsidiary MICTSI received a 25-year extension from PHIVIDEC Industrial Authority to operate the Mindanao Container Terminal in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, until 2058. MICTSI plans over USD 100m of investment including a 300 m berth extension and new equipment to grow capacity well beyond the current 350,000 TEU (target ~1m TEU by 2028).

title: ICTSI awarded 25-year concession for Iloilo Commercial Port Complex (Visayas Container Terminal)
summary: The Philippine Ports Authority granted ICTSI a 25-year concession to develop and operate the Iloilo Commercial Port Complex on Panay Island, renamed Visayas Container Terminal, with 627 m of quay and ~20 ha of yard; ICTSI committed to infrastructure upgrades and new cargo-handling equipment. By June 2026 the terminal had attracted Maersk's weekly PH6 service linking Iloilo to Yantian and Hong Kong.

title: ICTSI loses Puerto Caldera bid to APM Terminals/Hapag-Lloyd consortium, appeal triggers Comptroller review
summary: Costa Rica's INCOP awarded the 30-year concession for Puerto Caldera, the country's main Pacific port, to Consorcio Sunset (APM Terminals and Hapag-Lloyd) in March 2026. ICTSI, disqualified over a debt-to-equity calculation it disputes, appealed; the Comptroller General admitted the appeal and opened a review with a ruling expected within 40 business days. The current concession expires August 2026.

title: ICTSI starts operations at Batu Ampar Container Terminal, Batam
summary: ICTSI began operating the Batu Ampar Container Terminal in Batam, Indonesia, in September 2025, one of two new terminals (with Durban) that drove its 16% consolidated volume growth in H1 2026. Batam sits opposite Singapore and complements ICTSI's East Java Multipurpose Terminal at Lamongan (operational since October 2024), rebuilding its Indonesian footprint after exiting Jakarta.

title: ICTSI takes 47% of FII Inhauma fund for 32 ha ex-shipyard site next to ICTSI Rio
summary: ICTSI Americas B.V. acquired a 47% stake in the FII Inhauma real estate fund, securing perpetual rights over the 32 ha former Estaleiro Inhauma shipyard in Rio de Janeiro's Caju district adjacent to ICTSI Rio Brazil. Near term it adds yard space; long term ICTSI plans a private-use terminal (TUP). Terms undisclosed. In June 2026 ICTSI Rio also received two new quay cranes (total six) in a modernisation due 2029 that lifts capacity to 750,000 TEU.
capacity: 32 ha site; Rio terminal to 750,000 TEU by 2029

title: ICTSI's BCT Gdynia completes modernisation, handles largest ship in Polish history (MSC Venice, 16,652 TEU)
summary: Baltic Container Terminal Gdynia marked completion of its modernisation programme (new quay cranes, yard equipment, deepened harbour, rebuilt Helskie Quay, enlarged turning basin) with the maiden call of the 399 m MSC Venice, the largest vessel ever to berth in Gdynia. ICTSI was also shortlisted for the PLN 5bn Gdynia Outer Port PPP but did not submit a bid by the 30 Sep 2026 deadline, leaving TiL as sole bidder.

title: ICTSI H1 2026: volumes +16% to 8.12m TEU, recurring net income +25% to $605m, capex guidance $740m
summary: ICTSI reported H1 2026 revenue of USD 1.92bn (+27%), EBITDA USD 1.23bn (+24%), recurring net income USD 604.7m (+25%) and throughput of 8.12m TEU (+16%, +1% organic), driven by Durban Gateway Terminal and Batu Ampar. H1 capex was USD 320m with full-year guidance of USD 740m, ~90% for capacity at existing terminals in the Philippines, Mexico, Brazil, Australia, Ecuador, Honduras and DRC. Shows an operator in aggressive growth mode with strong balance sheet.

title: ICTSI FY2024: net income +66% to $850m on 13.07m TEU; 2025 capex plan $580m
summary: ICTSI's 2024 net income rose 66% to USD 849.8m (USD 830.9m excluding one-offs from legal settlements and Jakarta deconsolidation), revenue +15% to USD 2.74bn and consolidated volume +2% to 13.07m TEU despite the expired Karachi concession. The 2025 capex plan of USD 580m targeted expansions in the Philippines, Mexico and Brazil.

title: ICTSI keeps Umm Qasr (Basra Gateway) terminal running amid regional conflict; Middle East ~3% of throughput
summary: ICTSI's Christian Gonzalez told Bloomberg the group's Umm Qasr container terminal in southern Iraq had remained relatively calm despite escalating regional conflict, with staff safety the priority; the Middle East accounts for 2-3% of throughput and 3-4% of earnings. Higher insurance premiums and Suez rerouting were expected to raise freight rates. ICTSI earmarked ~USD 740m of 2026 capex, 90% for existing-terminal capacity, and continues to pursue acquisitions (Batam, Durban).
partners: General Company for Ports of Iraq

title: ICTSI's East Java Multipurpose Terminal (Lamongan) starts operations with bonded logistics facilities
summary: East Java Multipurpose Terminal, ICTSI's operation inside the Lamongan Shorebase complex, began handling containerised, bulk, project and heavy-lift cargo in October 2024, offering port, warehousing and bonded logistics facilities linked to the Jakamitra Industrial Park. In August 2026 it engaged East Java forwarders (ALFI) to build connectivity to Eastern Indonesia.

title: ICTSI's Toamasina concession runs to 2040 as $639m JICA-funded port expansion delivers new 756 m berth
summary: ICTSI's Madagascar International Container Terminal Services (operator since 2005) holds a 15-year extension of its Toamasina concession from October 2025 to 2040, signed in 2021 alongside a USD 639m port expansion (JICA USD 411m, Government USD 227m) adding a 756 m, -16 m berth for 14,000 TEU ships, a 15 ha yard and 400+ reefer plugs. Toamasina is the Indian Ocean island gateway where DP World has no presence.
capacity: 756 m berth, -16 m draught; 15 ha yard

title: CMA CGM to take 20% of Eurogate Container Terminal Hamburg; Western Extension to lift capacity to ~6m TEU
summary: CMA CGM signed a term sheet to acquire a 20% stake in Eurogate Container Terminal Hamburg (CTH, ~4m TEU/yr), becoming the third carrier to invest in a Hamburg terminal after MSC (HHLA) and COSCO (Tollerort); closing expected H1 2026 subject to approvals. CTH's Western Extension adds ~38 ha and ~1,050 m of quay, raising capacity to nearly 6m TEU. Marks Eurogate's shift from pure carrier-neutrality to carrier-anchored terminals to defend Hamburg volumes.
capacity: ~4m TEU today; ~6m TEU after Western Extension

title: Hapag-Lloyd's Hanseatic Global Terminals agrees to buy 20% of Eurogate CTH, making two carriers co-owners
summary: Hapag-Lloyd's terminal arm Hanseatic Global Terminals signed a term sheet to acquire a 20% stake in Eurogate Container Terminal Hamburg, so that CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd would each hold one-fifth, subject to approvals. In the same announcement Hapag-Lloyd agreed to raise its stake in Eurogate's Tanger Med TC3 terminal from 10% to 20%. The structure secures Gemini and Ocean Alliance volumes for Eurogate's Hamburg terminal against MSC-backed HHLA.

title: Hapag-Lloyd to double stake in Eurogate's Tanger Med TC3 terminal to 20%
summary: As part of its June 2026 terminal deals with Eurogate, Hapag-Lloyd's Hanseatic Global Terminals agreed to increase its shareholding in Eurogate Tanger (container terminal TC3 at Tanger Med) from 10% to 20%, subject to approvals. This deepens carrier anchoring at Eurogate's Western Mediterranean transhipment hub, which competes directly with MSC/TiL's planned Nador West Med terminal and with Algeciras.

title: APM Terminals and Eurogate unveil EUR 1bn plan to turn Bremerhaven's NTB into 4m TEU net-zero hub
summary: Joint owners APM Terminals and Eurogate entered advanced negotiations on a long-term arrangement to modernise North Sea Terminal Bremerhaven with ~EUR 1bn of investment: replacement and full electrification of yard and quay equipment on renewable power, making it Germany's first zero-direct-emission container terminal, with capacity rising from ~3m to ~4m TEU. Subject to internal and regulatory approvals; Bremen is pressing Berlin to deepen the Outer Weser. APMT CEO confirmed automation plans in May 2026.

title: Eurogate opens EUR 70m Rail Gate Bremerhaven intermodal terminal (330,000 containers/yr)
summary: Eurogate's new Rail Gate Bremerhaven, operating since 1 July 2025 and officially opened in July with Bremen's mayor and economics senator, has six 762 m tracks on 80,000 m2 and four remotely controlled gantry cranes, with capacity of up to 330,000 containers per year. The EUR 70m investment strengthens Bremerhaven's rail share (about half of local cargo) against Hamburg and Rotterdam hinterland competition.

title: Eurogate secures EUR 82m KfW IPEX loan for Wilhelmshaven automation pilot
summary: KfW IPEX-Bank granted Eurogate a EUR 82m loan to develop and test automated container handling at Container Terminal Wilhelmshaven: autonomous terminal trucks between quay and automated stacking cranes, Eurogate's in-house terminal management software and electrified equipment. Results will decide roll-out, with Hamburg first in line, then other German terminals. Signals Eurogate's catch-up on automation versus Rotterdam and HHLA.

title: Eurogate orders four Konecranes automated stacking cranes for Wilhelmshaven, option for four in Hamburg
summary: Eurogate Terminal Solutions ordered four Automated Stacking Cranes from Konecranes (booked Q3 2026) for automated yard handling at Container Terminal Wilhelmshaven, delivery Q2 2028, using a supplier-independent control architecture; the agreement includes an option for four more ASCs at Container Terminal Hamburg. First concrete equipment step of Eurogate's automation programme.

title: Eurogate Limassol approved to demolish warehouse for 15-20% more container storage
summary: Cyprus' Ministry of Transport approved Eurogate Container Terminal Limassol's plan to demolish an old warehouse inside the port, freeing 10,000-15,000 m2 for container storage, a ~EUR 1m self-funded project raising storage capacity by 15-20%, with works from early 2026 over about four months. Eurogate is also pushing a transit-trade strategy (100,000 TEU initially, potentially 400,000-500,000 TEU, ~EUR 40m extra investment) that would require amending its 2017 concession. Limassol is the port where DP World operates the multipurpose/cruise terminal next door.

title: Eurogate Limassol lobbies for transit-trade mandate, cites EUR 36m invested and EUR 40m plan
summary: Eurogate CTL's COO said the company has invested over EUR 36m since 2017 (yard expansion to ~12,000 TEU capacity, OCR, X-ray gate, Twin Sim AI yard tool, reefer system) and paid ~EUR 315m in concession fees, and wants government approval to handle transit cargo, which its 2017 agreement excludes: ~EUR 40m further investment to start at 100,000 TEU and scale to 400,000-500,000 TEU, positioning Limassol as the EU's last port versus non-EU Eastern Med hubs. In January 2026 the COO said transit flows from the Far East had begun.

title: Eurogate's new Damietta terminal (Damietta Alliance) recently opened, expected to grow significantly
summary: In an April 2026 interview, Eurogate CEO Michael Blach said the group's new terminal in Damietta, Egypt (the Damietta Alliance Container Terminal, with Hapag-Lloyd and Contship) had recently opened and was expected to grow significantly, as part of a network of 12 terminals targeting double-digit volume growth in 2026 (Q1 already double-digit). The Egyptian Mediterranean hub competes with Port Said and with DP World Sokhna for Egyptian gateway and transhipment cargo.

title: Eurogate CEO targets double-digit 2026 growth, open to Chinese carrier (COSCO/OOCL) terminal shareholding
summary: Eurogate CEO Michael Blach said the group (12 container terminals, hubs in Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven) plans double-digit volume growth for 2026 after regaining and exceeding the 25% of Hamburg volume lost in the 2017-18 alliance reshuffle, and that a shareholding partnership with a Chinese carrier such as COSCO or OOCL 'could very potentially' work at an existing or future terminal. He acknowledged ageing German terminals need modernisation and that ~50% of cargo moves by rail. Indicates openness to further carrier equity after CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd.
